elements.description:
How far a correction reaches: every artifact and released package that cites the corrected claim, each sent for
review – nothing rewritten automatically.

properties.name: heading
properties.description: The heading, and the component's name

properties.name: claim
properties.description: The claim as it was, before the correction

properties.name: meta
properties.description: Who corrected it and when, as one line – e.g. "Dana Okafor · today, 10:42"

properties.name: candidates
properties.description: The artifacts and released packages that cite the corrected claim

properties.name: states
properties.description:
Each item's state by id; an item not named here uses its own `state`, else "pending". Changed by the user unless a
tc-states-change listener calls preventDefault()

properties.name: note
properties.default: "Nothing is changed automatically – each item waits for a person."
properties.description: The line under the list – what the component won't do

properties.name: emptyText
properties.description: Shown when nothing cites the claim

properties.name: look
properties.description: Visual style: "standard" or "clean"; unset follows <tc-look-provider>, else "standard"

events.name: tc-states-change
events.description: An item's state changed ({ states, id, state, candidate }: CorrectionStatesChange – states is the whole new map); cancelable – prevent it to keep `states` as it is (controlled use)

events.name: tc-review
events.description: Review was pressed on an item ({ id, candidate }: CorrectionAction) – open it for a person to check

events.name: tc-supersede
events.description: Mark superseded was pressed on an item ({ id, candidate }: CorrectionAction)

events.name: tc-dismiss
events.description: Dismiss was pressed on an item – it doesn't rely on the claim ({ id, candidate }: CorrectionAction)

props.name: title
props.description: The heading, and the component's name

props.name: states
props.description: Each item's state by id. Controlled when defined; otherwise the component keeps it, starting at `defaultStates`

props.name: onStatesChange
props.type: (states: Record<string, CorrectionState>, id: string, state: CorrectionState) => void
props.description: Called with the whole new map, the item that changed and its new state

props.name: onReview
props.description: Review was pressed – open the item for a person to check

props.name: onDismiss
props.description: Dismiss was pressed – the item doesn't rely on the claim

changelog: **Trust & calibration**, from THEMIS and built domain-neutral: - claims and their reliability: `tc-claim-answer`, `tc-verification-queue`, `tc-reflection-gate`, `tc-reliance-gauge`, `tc-disagreement-banner`, `tc-synthesis-notes`; - where outputs came from: `tc-lineage-graph`, `tc-validity-badge`, `tc-provenance-summary`, `tc-correction-propagation`, `tc-attestation-check`, `tc-run-manifest`; - policy and control: `tc-policy-simulator`, `tc-gate-config`, `tc-coverage-matrix`, `tc-kill-switch`, `tc-playbook-canvas`.
